slides.say: Root two, over the bracket two plus root two. What does it equal?

slides: It's a fraction with a root on the bottom, and none of the choices is a fraction. So we need to get rid of the bottom. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, the math way, with algebra, and then with an estimate.

slides.say: In the roots topic we learned how. When the bottom is a sum with a root, we multiply the top and the bottom by its partner, called the conjugate. The partner of two plus root two is two minus root two. The top and the bottom are multiplied by the same thing, so it's like multiplying by one, and the value doesn't change.
at: we multiply the top and the bottom

slides.say: Why the partner? On the bottom we get two plus root two, times two minus root two. That's the difference of squares, a squared minus b squared. Two squared is four, and root two squared is two. Four minus two is two, so the root is gone.
On the top, root two times two is two root two. And root two times root two is two. So the top is two root two minus two.
So we have two root two minus two, over two. We divide each part by two, and we get root two minus one. Choice number four is our answer.
at: We divide each part by two
Choice number four is our answer

slides: Many students don't think of the partner here, and they get stuck. That's exactly when an estimate helps.

slides.say: [pause] Now the estimate. We don't need root two exactly. We only need to know between which numbers it is.
From the estimate we learned, root two is between one and two.
at: root two is between one and two

slides.say: We also narrowed that down: root two is between one and one and a half. We'll use these bounds to compare the choices.
at: root two is between one and one and a half

slides.say: Now the size of our fraction. The bottom is the top plus two, so the bottom is bigger than the top. That means the fraction is less than one.
at: The bottom is the top plus two

slides.say: Choice number two, two root two, is more than two, because root two is more than one. Choice number three, root two plus one, is also more than two. Both are more than one, so both are out.
at: Choice number two, two root two

slides.say: Two choices are left. Choice number four, root two minus one, is less than a half, because root two is less than one and a half.
at: Choice number four, root two minus one

slides.say: Choice number one is root two minus one, squared. Root two is between one and one and a half. So root two minus one is positive and less than a half. A half squared is a quarter. Squaring a smaller positive number gives less than a quarter. So choice number one is less than a quarter.
at: Choice number one is root two

slides.say: So is our fraction more than a quarter? The top, root two, is more than one. The bottom, two plus root two, is less than two plus two, which is four. A bigger top and a smaller bottom both make a fraction bigger. So the fraction is more than one over four, a quarter.
at: The top, root two, is more than one

slides.say: So choice number one is out, because it's less than a quarter. Choice number four is our answer again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: So choice number one is out
because it's less than a quarter
